jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
Environmental Specialist

Triumvirate Environmental, one of the largest environmental services firms in North America, is seeking an Environmental Specialist for our
Lab & Onsite Support Services (Lab/OSS)
team. As an Environmental Specialist, you will support our clients on-site by managing their hazardous waste programs & projects, utilizing state & federal regulations.  
Triumvirate Environmental provides leading organizations in the higher education, life sciences, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing sectors with diverse services and expertise to assist them with compliance management. At Triumvirate Environmental, we strive to WOW both our employees and our customers. Our unique culture fosters growth, development, education, and creativity.    
This position reports to the Regional Operations Manager. This role is based on site at client locations in the San Francisco Bay area
. You will report out of our
San Leandro, CA office.

We invite you to watch this video to discover more about the exciting responsibilities of an Environmental Specialist at Triumvirate Environmental.
CLICK HERE

Responsibilities:

Develop an understanding of OSHA regulations as well as Triumvirate’s Health and Safety practices 
Preparation of chemical and biological waste for shipment and disposal, including creation of all federal/state waste documents and managing the paperwork for the material. 
Safe handling of hazardous waste containers on client sites, as well as loading/unloading of waste from vehicles 
Conduct safety equipment and hazardous waste inspections. 
Occasionally perform and document Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) audits for clients. 
Deliver Exceptional Customer Service: Champion our commitment to the WOW! by providing outstanding support and innovative solutions to our clients 
Develop a high-level of state and federal regulatory expertise ensuring our client’s compliance needs are met (e.g RCRA, DOT, and OSHA) 
Conduct spill response measures, including the assessment of the spills and cleanup efforts 
Rotating on-call responsibilities as part of our Emergency Response team (optional)

Basic Requirements
:  
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in the hazardous-waste industry, or relevant military experience 
Ability to work as a member of a team as well as individually 
Must demonstrate strong verbal and written communication abilities to effectively interact with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders, ensuring clear and professional exchanges of information 
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues, develop solutions, and implement strategies to achieve positive outcomes 
Skilled in building strong, positive relationships with clients and colleagues 
Ability to work overtime on a regular basis 
Must be willing to work flexible hours within the work week (Monday through Friday) 
Ability to complete a 2 to 3 year professional advancement program in hazardous waste management 
The Environmental Specialist frequently handles hazardous chemicals and biological waste and is responsible for putting on and taking off personal protective equipment. This role is considered safety-sensitive 
Must be able to report to the office within 1 hour during Emergency Response rotating shifts  

Valid US driver’s license 
Must have a reliable form of transportation 
Must be willing to consent to Motor Vehicle Record screening, criminal background check, pre-employment physical, and drug screen (inclusive of THC) 
Upon employment, you will be required to participate in a random drug screening program (inclusive of THC) as part of our company’s commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy work environment 
Must be eligible to work in the United States without future sponsorship 
Must be able to lift 60 pounds on a regular basis 

Preferred Requirements:

Prior relevant industry experience 
Prior successful experience in a customer service role 
Active HAZWOPER 24 or 40 hour certification 
Willingness to obtain Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) 

Besides Health, Dental and Vision Insurance, we contribute to a 401k, offer a generous tuition reimbursement program, TONS of safety training for some positions with opportunities for external trainings and certifications, Mentorship & Career Succession Planning, Relocation Opportunities, Auto/Home insurance discounts, pet assistance discount plans, discounted movie passes & more!    
To learn more about our business, culture, and the exciting work that we are doing in the industry, find us on LinkedIn, Instagram (@triumvirateenvironmental), or our website !

jobs.title: Risk Assessment Privacy Specialist
jobs.description:
Ironwall by Incogni
is an executive privacy and protection service built for organizations that need to protect their most exposed people. We help companies and institutions reduce security risks to executives and other high-profile individuals by continuously finding and removing their personal information from the internet.

Role Overview

The Risk Assessment Specialist is responsible for conducting comprehensive Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) research to identify, analyze, and document publicly available information that may expose individuals to privacy, security, or personal safety risks.

This role involves researching multiple online sources, identifying personal information exposures, evaluating potential risks based on established assessment criteria, and developing detailed Risk Assessment reports that provide clients with a clear understanding of their digital exposure.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct OSINT research across search engines, data broker websites, people search platforms, public records, social media platforms, and other publicly accessible online sources.
Identify and document exposed personal information.
Analyze findings to determine potential privacy, security, and physical safety risks.
Evaluate exposure levels and assign risk scores based on established methodologies and guidelines.
Create comprehensive and well structured Risk Assessment reports, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and attention to detail.
Provide relevant insights and recommendations to help individuals understand and reduce their exposure.
Verify research findings and ensure all information included in reports is properly documented and supported by reliable sources.

Required Skills 

Strong online research and information-gathering capabilities.
Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Excellent analytical thinking and investigative research skills.
Ability to identify patterns and connections between different pieces of information.
Strong written communication skills.
Ability to interpret findings and assess potential risks.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently while following established processes and guidelines.
Understanding of online privacy, digital footprints, and information security is an advantage.

What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

The successful candidate is naturally investigative and enjoys connecting information across multiple sources. They are comfortable spending time researching, validating details, and identifying potential exposure risks that others might overlook.
They understand that seemingly unrelated pieces of publicly available information can collectively create meaningful privacy and security concerns. Most importantly, they can turn their research into accurate, organized, and actionable reports that help protect individuals.

Here's the deal:

Meaningful work:
Help protect people's personal information and reduce the risks of online exposure, fraud, cybercrime, and other threats.
Growth & development:
Join a growing company where you'll gain experience in privacy operations, online research, cybersecurity, and data protection.
Team environment:
Work remotely with a collaborative team that values ownership, accountability, and supporting one another.

Compensation:
MXN $300,000 per year plus benefits.

Ready to join us?

If you're detail-oriented, reliable, fluent in English, and passionate about protecting people's privacy, we'd love to hear from you.

Principal Scientist OR AD-level

Comp
175- 220k

Job Summary

The Project and Regulatory Toxicologist will be expected to use his/her toxicology expertise to guide safety assessment, design, and interpret in vitro/in vivo studies to evaluate the safety profiles of our covalently and non-covalently targeted small molecules according to regulatory guidelines. You will work closely with the toxicology function, CROs, and multidisciplinary drug discovery/development teams to progress promising therapeutics to the clinic.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Represent the toxicology function as a subject matter expert on drug discovery and development project teams, and provide guidance on the safety characterization, prioritization, and advancement of drug candidates
Directly interface with CROs to place appropriate in vitro and in vivo toxicology studies in a timely manner; manage and oversee the execution of toxicology studies at CROs to ensure high-quality data delivery; review and QC study protocols, results, and study reports; summarize toxicology study results and communicate findings to project teams and senior management accurately and punctually
Contribute to the writing of safety study summaries, nonclinical overviews, and other regulatory documents; represent the company at regulatory interactions
Identify and implement new strategies on safety assessment to address current and future safety-related challenges as needed; keep abreast of current regulatory requirements by participating in cross-industry consortia or scientific conferences
Collaborate with early discovery project teams to conduct literature-based target safety assessments and provide guidance on target safety derisking activities

Education and Experience Requirements
Ph.D. in pharmacology, toxicology, or a closely related biomedical discipline with 6+ years of industry experience, or M.S. in the above field with 10+ years of industry experience
Diplomate of the American Board of Toxicology is highly desired
A broad understanding of various aspects of nonclinical safety assessment and regulatory requirements for drug development; experience representing the toxicology function on discovery and development teams is required; expertise in immunology is highly desired
Must be able to critically evaluate, interpret, and integrate multidisciplinary data to support target and compound safety assessment and mechanistic derisking
Experience in the design, conduct, and data interpretation of in vitro and in vivo safety pharmacology, genetic toxicology, and general toxicology studies is required
Experience working with CROs

Required Key Attributes
Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact professionally and effectively in a dynamic, multidisciplinary, and highly collaborative team environment
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Solid problem-solving skills with a strong sense of urgency and scientific curiosity
Proactive and agile, with the ability to operate in a fast-paced work setting
Solution- and result-oriented with attention to detail

jobs.title: Principal Environmental Compliance Consultant
jobs.description:
Terraphase offers cost-effective solutions to complex environmental and engineering challenges. We listen to our clients and focus on their needs. We apply technical expertise and keen awareness of the regulatory framework to achieve our clients' project goals and objectives. The combined talent and experience of Terraphase's engineers, geologists, and scientists form the foundation for a comprehensive environmental management approach.

The Opportunity

Founded in 2010, Terraphase Engineering is a dynamic, privately owned environmental consulting firm seeking a Principal Environmental Compliance Consultant—Scientist, Geologist, or Engineer—with 18 or more years of professional experience to help lead, grow, and support our Compliance Services Division.

Compliance is one of Terraphase’s four core service areas, alongside Environmental, Site Engineering, and Water Resources. As one of our fastest-growing service areas, the division is central to Terraphase’s long-term growth strategy, with dedicated resources and leadership focused on expanding our capabilities and reach.

This is a senior leadership opportunity for a proven seller-doer who combines technical expertise, established client relationships, and sound business judgment. We are looking for a senior colleague to partner with our national compliance leadership, bring an active book of business, and take a meaningful role in serving and expanding Terraphase’s existing client base.

At Terraphase, you’ll enjoy the personal attention and entrepreneurial culture of a small-to-mid-sized firm with fewer than 200 people, supported by multidisciplinary resources and offices across the United States. You’ll have the opportunity to help shape strategy, develop your client portfolio, mentor emerging leaders, and deliver practical solutions that help clients manage risk, improve operations, and meet their environmental obligations.

A Flexible Senior-Level Role

We recognize that accomplished professionals may be looking for different ways to contribute at this stage of their careers. We welcome candidates seeking either full-time employment or a meaningful part-time leadership role.

The position may be based at any Terraphase office nationally. Candidates outside our existing office markets are also encouraged to apply; alternative locations and remote or hybrid arrangements will be considered where a mutually agreeable business and working arrangement can be established.

Much of the senior-level work involves technical direction, desktop review, client relationships, and team leadership. Responsibilities, availability, business development expectations, and project commitments will be aligned with the agreed schedule and role. Travel will be based on client, project, and team needs.

The Role

Partner with national compliance leadership to expand the practice, identify priority opportunities, and help shape its long-term growth strategy.
Maintain and grow an established portfolio of client relationships while actively supporting Terraphase’s existing clients and compliance programs.
Develop new business through professional relationships, referrals, industry engagement, and targeted pursuits, and identify opportunities to expand services within existing accounts.
Maintain comprehensive knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental requirements, including state-specific regulations in California, Washington, New Jersey, and Texas, and federal programs under the Clean Water Act, RCRA, Clean Air Act, EPCRA, and related authorities. Translate these requirements into practical compliance strategies for clients operating across multiple jurisdictions.
Lead large-scale, multisite, and multistate compliance programs, translating complex requirements into practical actions that fit client operations.
Serve as a trusted advisor to corporate leaders, environmental managers, and facility personnel, including guiding regulatory negotiations and agency interactions.
Direct projects involving compliance audits, gap analyses, discharge monitoring, hazardous waste and materials management, stormwater and wastewater, tank and spill prevention programs, air quality, litigation support, and permitting, consistent with your technical expertise.
Help clients prioritize findings, implement corrective actions, and develop effective approaches to ongoing compliance management.
Develop proposals, scopes of work, budgets, and schedules, and lead responses to small and large requests for proposals and statements of qualifications.
Support project bidding, contract solicitation, and pursuit strategy while maintaining realistic commitments for staffing, technical delivery, and profitability.
Oversee and mentor consultants, scientists, and engineers, and manage subcontractors and vendors.
Help project managers and emerging leaders develop their client management, business development, and technical leadership skills.
Provide quality assurance and technical review of reports, plans, specifications, and other deliverables.
Monitor regulatory developments and industry trends to anticipate client needs and identify appropriate service opportunities.
Collaborate across offices and disciplines to deliver coordinated, cost-effective solutions and connect clients with Terraphase’s broader capabilities.

Who You Are

You have 18 or more years of relevant professional experience focused on environmental compliance, including substantial experience in consulting. Candidates currently working in industry or other leadership roles who have prior consulting experience are welcome.
You hold a bachelor’s degree in engineering, geology, environmental science, or a related discipline.
You bring an established book of business and active client relationships, supported by a demonstrated record of generating and delivering consulting work.
You are interested in both developing your own client portfolio and taking responsibility for serving and growing an existing client base.
You have demonstrated success leading complex compliance programs, managing client portfolios, and balancing business development with project execution.
You offer recognized expertise in one or more environmental compliance disciplines and a strong understanding of federal and multistate regulatory frameworks.
You can connect technical recommendations with clients’ operational priorities, business objectives, and risk management needs.
You communicate effectively with clients, regulators, technical teams, and business leaders, including through proposals, presentations, and negotiations.
You are a collaborative leader who mentors others, shares opportunities across teams, and maintains high standards for technical quality, client service, and professional integrity.

Preferred Qualifications And Skills

Relevant professional licensure or certification, such as PE, PG, or CHMM, or demonstrated subject matter leadership in areas such as hazardous waste, stormwater, air quality, or other compliance disciplines.
Experience developing and managing national or regional client programs, including consistent approaches to compliance across multiple facilities.
Experience with environmental management systems, compliance tracking, or tools that help clients manage recurring obligations and corrective actions.
Familiarity with government platforms such as EPA CDX, CERS, RCRAInfo/myRCRAid, TRI-MEweb, ECHO, E-Plan, and similar compliance systems.
Familiarity with, or experience leading teams who use, ArcGIS, Power BI, AutoCAD, and comparable tools.
Participation in professional associations, technical presentations, or other activities that build industry relationships and demonstrate technical leadership.

Compensation for this position is based on years of experience, technical expertise, technical education, and geographic location.

Pay Range: $135,000 USD - $200,000 USD

Who We Are

We are an environmental consulting company that offers cost-effective solutions to complex environmental and engineering challenges. We apply technical expertise and keen awareness of the regulatory framework to achieve our clients' project goals and objectives. The combined talent and experience of Terraphase's engineers, geologists, and scientists form the foundation for a comprehensive environmental management approach.

Terraphase was founded with the goal of developing a full-service engineering and consulting firm that provides high-quality services to clients with regional and nationwide operations. We are driven by creating valuable work products for our company and clients, and a rewarding environment for our employees. Our staff is comprised of registered professionals in civil engineering, geology, hydrogeology, and geotechnical engineering.

Our unique company culture philosophy of appreciating and recognizing individuals for their work, leadership, and mentoring, while supporting and encouraging a healthy personal and professional lifestyle help to make Terraphase one of the best places to work.

Benefits

Terraphase offers an extensive benefits package including; Medical, Dental, Vision, Employer Paid Life Insurance, Long-Term Disability, a generous 401(k) match, Commuter Benefits, TerraLunches, TerraTalks, Tuition/Licensing/Professional Development Reimbursement, Flexible Work Schedule, ongoing company-sponsored events.

Provide quality assurance and technical review of reports, plans, specifications, and other deliverables.

Collaborate across offices and disciplines to deliver coordinated, cost-effective solutions and connect clients with Terraphase’s broader capabilities.

You bring an established book of business and active client relationships, supported by a demonstrated record of generating and delivering consulting work.
You are interested in both developing your own client portfolio and taking responsibility for serving and growing an existing client base.
You have demonstrated success leading complex compliance programs, managing client portfolios, and balancing business development with project execution.
You offer recognized expertise in one or more environmental compliance disciplines and a strong understanding of federal and multistate regulatory frameworks.
You can connect technical recommendations with clients’ operational priorities, business objectives, and risk management needs.
You communicate effectively with clients, regulators, technical teams, and business leaders, including through proposals, presentations, and negotiations.
You are a collaborative leader who mentors others, shares opportunities across teams, and maintains high standards for technical quality, client service, and professional integrity.

Preferred Qualifications And Skills

Relevant professional licensure or certification, such as PE, PG, or CHMM, or demonstrated subject matter leadership in areas such as hazardous waste, stormwater, air quality, or other compliance disciplines.
Experience developing and managing national or regional client programs, including consistent approaches to compliance across multiple facilities.
Experience with environmental management systems, compliance tracking, or tools that help clients manage recurring obligations and corrective actions.
Familiarity with government platforms such as EPA CDX, CERS, RCRAInfo/myRCRAid, TRI-MEweb, ECHO, E-Plan, and similar compliance systems.
Familiarity with, or experience leading teams who use, ArcGIS, Power BI, AutoCAD, and comparable tools.
